The usernames the channel carried out on a row while it was active

log_granted_names.Rd

For each of the channel's executions in the row's current life, log_executions(), the version that execution sealed, rebuilt from the log below it and verified by its seal, log_executed_row(); of those, the usernames of the versions whose request_status is not revoked. They are the names the channel gave an access to on this row: an execution of such a version brought its pair onto the instance. Not revoked rather than active, as register_to_desired() reads the field: a row imported without the state, which the form requires and the API does not, is served as active and sealed with the state empty (U8e of the review, 2026-11-12).

Usage

log_granted_names(events, record, channel_account)

Arguments

events

The owners' log, logtype = "record".

record

The record id.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the round's token, one or more. Not NULL: without them any account's seal would count.

Value

A character vector of usernames as carried out, each once (folded as addresses are); empty when the channel never carried the row out active, or the log does not say.

Details

What revocation_exits() asks, decided on 2026-11-12 after the review of unit G (RC1): the channel also seals a request withdrawn before its person was created, without asking any instance, and under the name the round would have created, a collision's proposal among them. That seal covers a name nobody was ever given, which may later be another person's; the row never granted it, and must not take it away. The guard of item 7, seal_holds_but_revocation(), asks the same question of the seal alone; here the name is asked too, so a revocation carried out together with another change (the role, say), whose revoked version was never sealed active, still finds the name it was given at an earlier execution.

A version the log does not verify names nobody: the answer can only be shorter, the direction that revokes less.
